findings.title: Under auto, an approved gate still reads as waiting for the human, so the driver stops there
quotes: status, command = f"waiting_for_human: approve {GATES[stage][0]}", f"nio flow done {stage} --commit {slug} --by human"
Stop on any `waiting_for_human`, `suspended`, or a printed `--commit` command
findings.fix: add a contract on `flow.py:where`: under auto, with no risky flag, a passing gate shows `working` with its `done` command, not `waiting_for_human: approve`. Add a TC that resumes a driver after the jury approved.

sources.situation: `where` sets this status when `ready == "pass"`, whatever `state["auto"]` is. A driver that takes over or resumes after a jury approved runs `nio flow next`, sees `waiting_for_human: approve spec` and a `--commit ... --by human` command, and stops (CT-16 step 4). Yet `done` would commit on its own under auto for a spec with no risky flag. No contract changes `where`, so a non-risky auto run stops at every gate it re-enters after approval. That breaks NFR-2 and AC-11.

findings.reason: flow.py:700 sets `waiting_for_human: approve` whenever `ready == "pass"`, whatever `auto` is, and no contract changes `where`. CT-16 step 4 stops on that status. TC-11 only calls `done` directly, so no test resumes a driver after the jury approved.
findings.note: CT-20 where shows working under auto; TC-49

| `rejected` | dispose of each open finding (step 4), fix the artefact, then call the step again |
`spec-fix` that changes behaviour | the human, through @nio:grill

sources.situation: the driver runs the jury skill in a subagent (FR-6). That skill follows its own Decide table: it disposes and fixes `--by agent`, and grills the human on a behaviour change. Nothing in it says to hand `rejected` to `nio-fixer` or to use `--by auto`/`held`. CT-19 changes only the skill's flow-state line, while CT-18 gives the grill a `## Under auto` section. Under auto, the fixer card and the `held` path would never run, and the run would go back to the human or fix as `agent`.

findings.reason: skills/jury/SKILL.md step 4 (lines 101-106) still disposes `--by agent` and grills the human on behaviour changes. CT-19 touches only its flow-state line, and plan.md has no contract for a jury-skill `## Under auto`. CT-16's one sentence is a driver instruction, not a change to the skill the subagent follows.

findings.title: The driver claim identifies its holder by the `--by` string, which two sessions share
quotes: a claim whose `by` equals the caller's is refreshed (`at` rewritten)
mine = (os.getpid(), host, datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat())
if missing := [x for x in ("flow.lock*", "state.json.new") if x not in have]:
findings.fix: put a per-driver nonce in the claim, created on the first `drive`, printed by `drive` and passed back on each refresh and on `--release`. Refresh only on a matching nonce. Add `driver.lock*` to `.gitignore`. Add a TC with two drivers that pass the same `--by`.

sources.situation: `lock`, the code CT-5 is `Like:`, identifies its holder by pid and host. CT-5 identifies the holder by `--by "<role> / <host> / <model>"`. Two Claude Code sessions on the same model both pass the same string, so the second "refreshes" the first's claim and both drive, which is what FR-29 forbids. The tests hide this because they use `driver / a / m` and `driver / b / m`. Also, CT-5 renames to `driver.lock.<pid>.<hex>` but only adds `driver.lock` to `.gitignore`. A crash leaves the temp file for `commit_gate`'s `git add -A` to commit. `lock` ignores `flow.lock*` for this reason.

two driver sessions on the same host and model, both started with the same `by` string (role / host / model). The first claims the effort. The second calls `nio flow drive`. Its `by` equals the claim's `by`, so CT-5 refreshes the claim and the second driver carries on. Both now move the effort, and AC-9 / FR-29 say the second must stop. The only refusal is the `O_EXCL` race loser, so a late second driver is never refused. The `by` is a role / host / model string, not a session identity, so it cannot separate two drivers.

the human, or a compacted session's replacement, starts a second `@nio:auto` on the same machine and model. Both pass `--by "driver / claude-code / <model>"`. The second call matches `by`, so CT-5 refreshes the claim instead of refusing it. Two drivers then run `next`/`done` and two fixers edit `spec.md` at the same time. `flow.lock` serialises history writes but not the fixers' file edits, so one fixer's edits silently overwrite the other's. TC-9, TC-43 and TC-44 all use distinct `by` strings, so no test shows the collision.

findings.reason: CT-5 refreshes a claim whose `by` equals the caller's, and `by` is "<role> / <host> / <model>", which two sessions can share. TC-9, TC-38 and TC-43 use distinct `by` strings. The `driver.lock*` ignore point overlaps ledger J-12.
findings.note: CT-5 per-driver token, temp-file refresh, driver.lock* ignored; TC-51, TC-38

findings.title: CT-7 binds `resumed`, which can't write the `raise` line it describes
quotes: when the state is `auto` and the pause it clears is `suspended: cap` or `suspended: stuck`, the `resume` line is followed by
entry, new = resumed(state, lines, None, stop if stop and stop["kind"] == "pause" else None)
return line, {**state, "pause": None, "abandon": None, "waiting": None}
findings.fix: bind CT-7 to `flow.py:start` (existing). Once `entry["to"]` is known, append the `raise` line with the gate read from the cleared pause, or from `GATES[entry["to"]]`. Keep `resumed`'s return shape.

sources.situation: `resumed` returns one line and the state. `start`, the caller that resumes a cap or stuck suspension, passes stage `None` and sets `entry["to"]` only afterwards. So inside `resumed`, the `raise` line's `from`/`to` and `evidence.gate` ("the stage's gate") are unknown. If it is written there, the gate is `""` and the stopped gate's round limit never rises, which breaks AC-41 and TC-41's "at plan round 4 no round pause".

findings.reason: CT-7 binds `resumed`, and `start` calls it with stage None (flow.py:892) and sets `entry["to"]` afterwards. CT-7's own "stage's gate or ''" lets an empty gate be written, and `stops` counts raise lines per gate. TC-41 would catch it, but the contract binds the wrong function.

quotes: Observable: the grant line's `who` holds a non-empty host and model.
return {"role": "human", "host": "", "model": ""}

sources.situation: CT-1's grant goes through `record` with `who("human")`, whose host and model are always empty. The host and model go to `evidence.ran_in` instead, and TC-42 checks `evidence.ran_in`. AC-42 as written then always fails, though the plan's decision says it is kept as written.

CT-1 and the architecture put the host and model in `evidence.ran_in` and leave `who` as the human. They also store the literal `unknown` when nothing is detected. A test written from AC-42 reads `who` and fails. A test written from CT-1 reads `ran_in` and passes with `unknown`, which satisfies AC-42's "non-empty" without recording a host or model, so FR-30's audit trail can be empty and still pass.

findings.reason: AC-42's Observable says the grant's `who` holds host and model, but `who("human")` (flow.py:48-51) gives empty host and model, and CT-1 and TC-42 use `evidence.ran_in`. The plan says it keeps AC-42 "as written", which is false.

findings.title: After the human accepts a round-check hit, nothing can start the next round
quotes: a CT-13 hit while `current` differs from the judged version → `human` with CT-13's lines
and no `resume` line names this gate and round → `pause`
findings.fix: tell CT-12 and CT-13 how the human's acceptance is recorded, so the hit clears once a resume line names the gate and round and `composed` falls through to `compose`'s `rerun`. The same applies to `held` once the human re-disposes it. Add an AC for resuming after a CT-13 hit.

sources.situation: a fix round removes AC-4. The round ends with `current` different from the judged version. CT-12 composes `human`, and CT-6 item 1 pauses. The human reads it, accepts the cut and resumes with `nio flow start`. A resume line now names this gate and round, so `stops` does not pause again. But no new round has been collected, so `current` still differs from the judged version, and `composed` returns `human` with the same CT-13 lines on every call, before `compose` could return its own `rerun` ("changed since round N judged it"). `rerun` is the only outcome that makes the jury skill run the lenses. The driver and the jury skill therefore get `human` forever. The only exits are `--human` closure of the gate, which skips the re-review, or the human running a round by hand. The same loop applies to a `held` finding after the human resumes without re-disposing it. Spec UJ-2 says the human "settles it and resumes; the run carries on in auto".

findings.reason: CT-12 returns `human` for a CT-13 hit for as long as `current` differs from the judged version, ahead of `compose`'s `rerun` (jury.py:1014). A resume line only silences CT-6 item 1. Nothing clears the hit, so UJ-2's "settles it and resumes; the run carries on" has no path.
findings.note: CT-12 resume line naming gate and round clears a round-check hit; re-disposed held clears; TC-52

findings.title: The human's draft is rewritten with no committed copy to restore
quotes: remove `## Open points`, move each OP ID to `retired`
The git blob hash of `text`, stored in git's objects when `write` (the version a round judged, #27 FR-23).
`## Fixed by the run`: each finding with `by: auto`: `- J-n [<severity>] <title>: <note> (<gate>, verdict <V-id>)`;
findings.fix: commit (or stash on `nio/<slug>`) the effort folder as it stands at the grant, before the grill or the fixer edit anything, and have the grill's `## Auto` entry copy each removed open point's text. Add a TC that grants auto, runs the grill and one fixer round, then recovers the original `spec.md` from the grant commit.

sources.situation: the human writes a draft and grants auto at drafting. The grill under auto deletes `## Open points` and retags items before any jury round, so no version of the draft before the grill is stored anywhere. The grill.md entry keeps only "each choice and its reason", not the open point's text. Later fixer edits survive only as `hash-object -w` blobs, which are referenced by the ledger but by no commit, so `git gc` can prune them. CT-13 also depends on those blobs. The run report gives a note per fix, not the text before it. A human who disagrees with an `[auto]` choice or a fix has no reliable way to get their own wording back, and no TC tries.

findings.reason: The human's own words are protected by FR-10, FR-12 and CT-13's `[human]` checks. What the grill removes are open points that become `[auto]` items listed with IDs in CT-14's report, and each fix has a note and a verdict. Nothing in the spec requires restoring open-point text, so this is a wish rather than an allowed bad outcome.

findings.title: Claim takeover leftovers aren't ignored, and refresh skips the takeover's re-check

findings.fix: add `driver.lock*` to the ignore list, and write refreshes to a temp file then `os.replace` after re-reading that the claim still names the caller. TC-38 can also assert that `.gitignore` holds `driver.lock*`.

sources.situation: `lock` ignores `flow.lock*`, a glob, but CT-5 adds the bare name `driver.lock`. A driver that dies between the rename and the unlink leaves `driver.lock.<pid>.<hex>`, which the next auto approval commit adds to the effort folder's commit. Separately, a refresh rewrites `at` in place on a `by` match. If it races a takeover, which renames, re-reads and creates, the refresh can write over the new holder's claim, or leave a torn file that no reader parses.

sources.situation: An effort is granted auto at grilling. The grill deletes `## Open points` from `spec.md` and logs only its choices. Nothing has committed `spec.md` yet, and no jury round has stored a version of it. The human then switches auto off to answer OP-3 themselves. The original question and its options are gone from the spec, from git and from `grill.md`. If the grill stops halfway (OP-1 is now an item but not yet in `retired`), a re-run can turn OP-1 into a second item.

findings.reason: The grill turns open points into `[auto]` items that the spec jury judges and the report lists (CT-14, FR-14), and FR-14 says switching auto off reopens none of them, so the "answer OP-3 myself" path is not promised. Nothing requires keeping the original open-point text, as the ledger's J-11 refutation says. The mid-grill re-run duplicate is speculative, because the CT-18 text does not describe a non-idempotent flow.
